component.name: Unswiper
component.summary: Sort trip photos into visits, keep the best, set aside the rest

description.p: Unswiper groups the photos and videos in a folder into visits by date, lets you mark each one Keep or Reject with the keyboard, and moves the rejects to the Trash or a quarantine folder only when you commit. Every commit can be undone.

ul.li: Works on any folder; nothing is uploaded
HEIC, JPEG, PNG, RAW sidecars and videos
Watches the folder and updates live
Restore Last Commit puts files back

description.p: Arrow keys move the selection in the photo grid. Mac: no more crash when resizing the window with Photo Info open, and the photos keep their room next to Photo Info.

The large view shows each photo's blur score, and the Low, Normal and High blur cutoffs can be edited. Switching visits or grouping returns to the grid. Fixes a GTK warning when right-clicking photos.
Large libraries stay responsive: indexing and the blur check run in the background with progress bars, Cancel, Pause and Stop, and the photo grid only builds what is on screen.

Group by place: choose By Visit (Time), By Place (all photos from one town together) or By Visit and Place (each trip split per town), with offline place names. Photos without a camera date get one from GPS time or the file name, and visits are listed oldest first.

Import from Google Photos: a step-by-step assistant explains which Google Takeout options to pick, checks free space, unpacks your exports with a progress bar (stop and continue later) and uses Google's dates and places.

Photo Info: see the camera, lens, shutter, aperture, ISO, date, size and (optionally) location of a photo or video, with a quick look on right-click and a full panel (I or Ctrl+I). AppImage: videos play on newer distributions, and AVI, MPG and 3GP videos are supported.

Blurry photo detection: likely out-of-focus or shaken photos are marked Reject with a Blurry? badge (nothing moves until you commit; your choices always win). Play videos and Live Photo motion in a full-window viewer (Space or double-click). AppImage bundles audio playback.
First Linux release: GTK 4 app on the shared Rust core, as Flatpak and AppImage. Video thumbnails via GStreamer, HEIC via libheif, new icon. Commit applies only to the open visit.
